Redwood kickoff with Copperridge to align on onboarding milestones, network/VPC requirements, security checklist, and pilot scope for search and ai-assist. Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya Patel from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We wanted to kick off the onboarding and make sure we align on success criteria, network steps, and the pilot scope.
[00:14] Tom: Yeah, thanks. We've been excited to get started. I think Sara and Marcus will drive the hands-on bits.
[00:19] Sara: Hi all — Sara here. Quick context: we've got a small MLOps squad and a platform team who'll handle infra. Pilot goal is to embed ai-assist into our agent tools and improve internal triage search.
[00:30] Jonas: Great — I'm Jonas, Customer Success. I'll be your main runway coordinator, scheduling, and making sure the playbook checks off.
[00:36] Marcus: Marcus — platform eng. We'll need the VPC details, and someone from net/security to sign off.
[00:41] Priya: Priya, security. We'll want SOC-2 artifacts, key management detail, and clarity on log retention.
[00:47] Eddie: Eddie from Redwood SE — I'll run the technical onboarding, perf checks, and the POC runbook. Quick question up front: are you planning hosted API or dedicated capacity?
[01:00] Tom: Initially hosted, but we'd like an option for dedicated if latency or compliance push us.
[01:06] Maya: That's common. For the pilot hosted is fastest. If you need reserved throughput we can scope Dedicated — we'll cover what triggers that.
[01:12] Sara: Can you outline the network pattern? We are strict about egress rules.
[01:17] Eddie: Sure. High-level — we support a VPC peering approach or private link depending on cloud. We'll send a network diagram. You provide CIDR ranges and firewall contacts. Also note that some of our internal names get weird in transcription — sometimes 'K-V cache' shows up as the 'K V cash' — so just to be clear, we mean KV cache / prefix caching.
[01:36] Marcus: Cool. We'll map that. Do you need route tables changed?
[01:40] Eddie: For peering, usually not. For private link, there are a few NAT/route considerations. We'll include both options in the diagram.
[01:47] [00:02:00] Jonas: Onboarding playbook — we'll cover staging, load tests, and go-live checklist. We'll also include a rubric for success metrics. Sara, what's your top success metric?
[02:05] Sara: For the search piece, precision of returned results and mean time to resolution for agents — target reduction of ~25% in triage time.
[02:12] Tom: For product it's lower latency (p95) under 300ms for the UI flows — that's our rule of thumb.
[02:20] Eddie: That's helpful. We'll propose a config that balances batching to keep cost sensible while hitting the p95. There's a trade-off we can tune — quantization and continuous batching.
[02:30] Priya: On encryption and keys — do you integrate with our KMS or do you host keys?
[02:36] Maya: For Redwood Private deployments we can do customer-managed keys and HSM integrations. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can provide SOC2 docs; we'll attach the detailed security pack.
[02:47] Priya: OK send the compliance pack. Also SCIM provisioning — can you support automatic user provisioning from our IdP?
[02:54] Jonas: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll include the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the playbook.
[03:01] Marcus: Who handles audit logging and retention? We need 12 months of immutable logs for audit.
[03:07] Eddie: Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via secure forwarding; retention's flexible. We'll propose default retention and show how to push logs to your storage.
[03:14] [00:03:00] Sara: About pilot scope — we want two flows: search ranking rerank for internal docs, and a contextual ai-assist for agents. Minimal viable integration for the pilot?
[03:25] Eddie: For MVP: endpoint calls from your backend to Redwood API, use a curated model from our catalog, enable prefix caching for repeated queries, and validate outputs against your prompt set. We'll provide a sample relay integration for the agent UI.
[03:39] Tom: How long does onboarding usually take for this kind of pilot?
[03:44] Jonas: Typically 2–4 weeks to a working pilot if network/firewall approvals are fast, otherwise add a week for enterprise approvals. 
[03:52] Sara: Our security team needs to review the playbook before we approve staging.
[03:56] Maya: Understood. We'll send playbook and the security artifact pack by Thursday (2026-12-16). Please highlight any blocking items and we'll set an escalation path.
[04:07] [00:04:00] Priya: Also need clarity on data residency. Some of our logs have PII; can you guarantee that logs with PII stay in region?
[04:15] Maya: We have region pinning and data residency options for Private deployments. For hosted, we can route to region and provide options for minimal retention. We'll outline specifics in the security doc.
[04:26] Marcus: Regarding metrics — we want token-level cost estimates. Can you provide tooling to estimate token usage per request pattern?
[04:33] Eddie: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token breakdown per request and model. For pilot we can run simulated traffic and provide projected cost based on your query distribution.
[04:44] Tom: Is there a sandbox we can use with our prompts before hitting production?
[04:48] Jonas: Yes — staging environment with feature flags. We'll provide API keys that are scoped to staging and limited throughput for testing.
[04:55] [00:05:00] Sara: A couple of nitty-gritty items — rate limits, retry behavior, and error handling patterns. We have to bake that into our agent UI.
[05:04] Eddie: We'll include recommended retry/backoff config, and best practices for fallback behavior — e.g., return cached answer or degrade to basic keyword search.
[05:13] [00:06:00] Marcus: On the technical side, for large context windows — do you recommend chunking or retrieval-augmented generation?
[05:20] Eddie: Retrieval-augmented generation is typically best for long docs; chunking plus rerank for relevance. We'll share an RAG pattern and an example pipeline in the runbook.
[05:30] Sara: For evaluation — we want to run weekly quality checks during pilot. Can Redwood help with automated evals?
[05:37] Maya: Yes, we have a quality-monitoring feature and can run regression alerts tied to your prompt sets. We'll set up an initial eval harness with your sample queries.
[05:48] [00:07:00] Tom: Regarding SLOs — what uptime and latency guarantees do you provide for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:55] Maya: Hosted has standard SLOs (we'll include specifics). Dedicated comes with stricter SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; the commercial team can provide a formal SLA if you move to Dedicated.
[06:05] Priya: We'd like an escalation matrix if the pilot hits a security incident.
[06:09] Jonas: We'll add a contact list and escalation path in the runbook; add redwood security and CSM contacts.
[06:15] [00:08:00] Eddie: Quick note — sometimes transcription shows 'Redwood Dei' or other mis-reads in notes; ignore that. Real product names: Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private.
[06:26] Marcus: Good to clarify. Ok, can you walk briefly through the staging runbook steps?
[06:31] Eddie: Sure. Step 1: network connectivity confirmed (CIDRs, peering, firewall). Step 2: staging credentials and API keys provisioned. Step 3: small smoke test — health checks, token usage sanity. Step 4: performance test (50–200 qps depending on pilot). Step 5: quality evaluation and sign-off. We'll attach a checklist in the playbook.
[06:55] Sara: For performance, can you simulate our peak agent load? We have bursts up to 150 qps during morning peak.
[07:03] Eddie: Yes, we can run load simulations and adjust batching and cache. For 150 qps bursts we might recommend a small Dedicated pool or burst capacity depending on latency needs.
[07:14] [00:09:00] Tom: Any blockers from Redwood side we should know?
[07:18] Maya: Just the usual — need CIDR ranges, firewall contact, and security review sign-off. Once we have those, the SE can start the runbook and demo flows.
[07:27] Priya: We'll compile the compliance questions. Also, can we get an anonymized security whitepaper?
[07:32] Jonas: We'll attach the SOC2 and architecture whitepaper in the follow-up.
[07:37] Sara: About the pilot timeline — when can we expect a working staging demo?
[07:41] Jonas: If we get network details by 12/16 and the security review doesn't block, we can target a staging demo by 12/29. That gives two weeks for integration and testing.
[07:52] [00:10:00] Marcus: One last infra question: do you have terraform modules or IaC snippets for quick provisioning?
[07:58] Eddie: Yes, we provide Terraform snippets for peering, IAM roles, and service accounts. We'll include a repo link in the playbook.
[08:07] Tom: Any specific logging format? We push to Splunk — can you forward logs there?
[08:12] Eddie: Yes, we can forward via secure endpoint or S3 ingestion — flexible. We'll include examples for Splunk HEC.
[08:22] [00:11:00] Jonas: OK let's recap roles and next steps — Maya to send playbook + network diagram; Marcus to provide CIDR ranges and FW contact; Eddie to prepare POC runbook and perf checklist; Sara to assemble pilot prompts and success metrics; Priya to compile compliance questions. We'll target the staging demo by 12/29.
[08:44] Maya: That matches my notes. Anything else?
[08:48] Priya: One more — data deletion policy for test data. We want the ability to purge test logs after the pilot.
[08:54] Maya: We'll document deletion policies and retention controls.
[08:57] [00:12:00] Tom: Great. Also curious about pricing ballpark for pilot vs production dedicated.
[09:02] Maya: We'll include rough estimates in the playbook and a separate pricing sheet — pilot minimal cost, production depends on model choice, quantization, and throughput.
[09:14] Sara: If we hit 1M tokens/day, what's the likely path?
[09:18] Eddie: At that scale we'd recommend model optimizations, aggressive caching, and possibly dedicated pools to control latency and cost. We'll model that for you.
[09:26] [00:13:00] Jonas: I'll create a CRM deal and put calendar invites for the SE workshop and staging demo.
[09:31] Marcus: Thanks. For the SE workshop, can we add our infra lead?
[09:34] Jonas: Please do.
[09:36] [00:14:00] Closing minutes:
Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the playbook, security artifacts, and the Terraform snippets. Expect docs by 2026-12-16. Jonas will schedule the SE deep-dive for early January, and we'll aim for the staging demo on 2026-12-29 pending approvals.
Tom: Sounds good — appreciate it.
Sara: Thanks, talk soon.
Marcus: Thanks.
Priya: Bye.
Eddie: Bye.
